s1.syndrome_frame: Acute scrotal pain and swelling in a pediatric patient
salient_findings: Enlarged testis, epididymis, and infected appendages
Purulent foci on the surface of the sperm vessels
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with a five-day history of left scrotal soreness and oedema
No lower urinary tract symptoms
No major relevant medical or surgical history
Occult penis diagnosed based on penile characteristics
Other congenital anomalies of the genitourinary tract excluded based on imaging findings
Mild leukocytosis (18.5 × 10^9/L) on blood workup
Urine analysis was negative
Pus culture isolated P. aeruginosa, susceptible to ceftazidime and ofloxacin
Doppler ultrasonography showed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern and enhanced vascularity
Follow-up sonography showed heterogeneous echotexture in the left testis and epididymis
MRI at 60 days showed no enhancement in T2, indicating disappearance of the left testis
Pathological examination showed hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage and fibrocystic-like tissue with inflammatory cell infiltration

shortlist.label: Epididymitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with scrotal soreness and oedema, and imaging studies showed an enlarged epididymis

shortlist.label: Orchitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had an enlarged testis with heterogeneous echo pattern and enhanced vascularity on Doppler ultrasonography

shortlist.label: Appendicitis of the testis
shortlist.why_kept: Pathological examination showed hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage

shortlist.label: Scrotal cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had scrotal soreness and oedema, and pus culture isolated P. aeruginosa

shortlist.label: Tuberculous epididymitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had chronic inflammation and fibrocystic-like tissue with inflammatory cell infiltration on pathological examination

raw.rationale: The patient presented with scrotal soreness and oedema, and imaging studies showed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern and enhanced vascularity, indicating inflammation of the testis. The presence of mild leukocytosis and purulent foci on the surface of the sperm vessels also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Epididymitis
rejected.why: While the epididymis was also affected, the primary issue seemed to be with the testis, as indicated by the imaging findings and the pathological examination.

rejected.label: Appendicitis of the testis
rejected.why: The pathological examination did show hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage, but the primary clinical presentation and imaging findings pointed more towards orchitis.

rejected.label: Scrotal cellulitis
rejected.why: The presence of purulent foci and leukocytosis suggests a more localized infection rather than a diffuse cellulitis.

rejected.label: Tuberculous epididymitis
rejected.why: There is no indication of tuberculosis in the provided information, and the isolated organism was P. aeruginosa, not Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

gold: Acute epididymal orchitis with testicular infarction caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
